s: The Agreement on Agriculture (AoA) rests on which of the following three pillars?
o: Domestic support, market access and export competition
Market access, investment protection and government procurement
Export competition, services and industrial subsidies
Domestic support, intellectual property and trade facilitation
x: The AoA has three pillars: domestic support, market access and export competition.
tq: Identify the standard three-part structure of the agreement.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with Blue Box support under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Research expenditure with no production connection
Direct payments linked to unlimited expansion of production
Direct payments under production-limiting programmes
All subsidies prohibited under the SCM Agreement
x: Blue Box support consists of direct payments connected with production-limiting programmes. Although trade-distorting, such support is exempt from reduction commitments.
tq: Distinguish the production-limiting feature of the Blue Box from Green and Amber categories.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: With reference to Amber Box subsidies, which of the following statements is correct?
o: They are direct payments that limit production and are exempt from all reductions.
They include price- or quantity-linked support such as MSP and input subsidies, measured through AMS.
They are support measures unrelated to prices or quantities and therefore have no limits.
They refer only to export subsidies paid to least developed countries.
x: Amber Box support covers price- or quantity-linked measures, including MSP, power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation subsidies. Such support is trade-distorting and is measured as Aggregate Measurement of Support (AMS).
tq: Use the examples of price and input support to identify the Amber Box.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT an official subsidy box under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Green Box
Amber Box
Red Box
Blue Box
x: Green, Blue and Amber are the subsidy boxes under the AoA. Red, Orange and Yellow are not AoA boxes; a prohibited-subsidy category described as a red-light category belongs to the SCM context.
tq: Find the odd term in a closely related list of official categories.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: The de minimis limit for Amber Box support is generally what percentage of the value of agricultural output for developing countries?
o: 5 per cent
10 per cent
15 per cent
20 per cent
x: Developing countries are allowed Amber support up to 10 per cent of the value of agricultural output under the de minimis provision.
tq: Recall the country-category distinction in a percentage-based provision.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: The de minimis limit for Amber Box support applicable to developed countries is:
o: 15 per cent of agricultural output
10 per cent of agricultural output
2 per cent of agricultural output
5 per cent of agricultural output
x: For developed countries, Amber support within 5 per cent of the value of agricultural output is allowed without penalty under the de minimis provision.
tq: Compare the two country-specific thresholds rather than reversing them.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: Under the market-access commitments of the Agreement on Agriculture, developed countries were required to reduce tariffs by 36 per cent over six years, whereas developing countries were required to reduce them by:
o: 36 per cent over ten years
12 per cent over five years
24 per cent over ten years
30 per cent over eight years
x: The specified commitment for developing countries was a 24 per cent tariff reduction over ten years, compared with 36 per cent over six years for developed countries.
tq: Match both the percentage and time period instead of relying on one figure alone.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: The conversion of non-tariff agricultural barriers into tariffs under the Agreement on Agriculture is known as:
o: Countervailing
Tariffication
Harmonisation
Graduation
x: Tariffication means converting non-tariff barriers into tariff equivalents as part of the market-access commitments.
tq: Identify the exact technical term for a policy process.
sec: Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access  [APPSC]

s: The highest decision-making body of the World Trade Organization is required to meet:
o: Only when requested by the Director-General
At least once every two years
Every year without exception
Once in five years
x: The WTO Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body and meets at least once every two years under the Marrakesh Agreement.
tq: Recall the institutional hierarchy and minimum meeting frequency.

s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding WTO Ministerial Conferences:

List-I (Conference)
a. First Ministerial Conference
b. Second Ministerial Conference
c. Third Ministerial Conference
d. Fourth Ministerial Conference

List-II (Venue and year)
i. Seattle, 1999
ii. Singapore, 1996
iii. Doha, 2001
iv. Geneva, 1998

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii
a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i
a–ii, b–i, c–iv, d–iii
a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii
x: MC1 was held at Singapore in 1996, MC2 at Geneva in 1998, MC3 at Seattle in 1999 and MC4 at Doha in 2001.
tq: Start from the sure venue-year pair and eliminate codes.

s: Which of the following was associated with the First WTO Ministerial Conference held at Singapore in 1996?
o: The adoption of the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
The launch of the Doha Development Agenda
The Singapore issues and the Information Technology Agreement
The beginning of the e-commerce customs-duty moratorium
x: The Singapore Ministerial Conference introduced the Singapore issues—investment, competition, procurement transparency and trade facilitation—and was associated with the Information Technology Agreement.
tq: Link a conference with its distinctive outcome rather than its venue alone.

s: The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium was begun at which WTO Ministerial Conference?
o: MC9, Bali, 2013
MC1, Singapore, 1996
MC2, Geneva, 1998
MC4, Doha, 2001
x: The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium began at the Second Ministerial Conference in Geneva in 1998.
tq: Discriminate between successive early Ministerial Conferences using their outcomes.

s: The Third WTO Ministerial Conference at Seattle in 1999 is remembered chiefly because it:
o: Collapsed amid protests
Adopted the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement
Ended agricultural export subsidies
Adopted the Bali Package
x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 collapsed amid protests.
tq: Associate a highly distinctive event with the correct conference.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Fourth WTO Ministerial Conference held at Doha in 2001?
o: The Bali Package and interim Peace Clause were adopted.
The e-commerce moratorium was begun and the Singapore issues were introduced.
The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted.
The Doha Development Agenda was launched and a TRIPS-public health declaration was adopted.
x: The Doha Conference launched the Doha Development Agenda and adopted the declaration concerning TRIPS and public health.
tq: Use the conference’s signature agenda and declaration to identify the correct option.

s: The Fifth WTO Ministerial Conference at Cancun in 2003 ended with which of the following developments?
o: It collapsed over agriculture and Singapore issues, and the G-33 was formed.
It eliminated agricultural export subsidies.
It adopted the Doha Development Agenda and the TRIPS-public health declaration.
It adopted the COVID-related TRIPS waiver.
x: The Cancun Ministerial Conference collapsed over agriculture and Singapore issues, and the G-33 was formed in that context.
tq: Avoid confusing the Cancun outcome with the outcomes of Doha and Nairobi.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Sixth WTO Ministerial Conference at Hong Kong in 2005:
1. It included a commitment to end farm export subsidies.
2. It addressed duty-free and quota-free access for least developed countries.
3. It adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: The Hong Kong Ministerial Conference dealt with ending farm export subsidies and duty-free, quota-free access for LDCs. The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement was adopted much later at MC12 in 2022.
tq: Reject the later-outcome trap by placing each development in its conference year.

s: The WTO Ministerial Conferences held at Geneva in 2009 and 2011 were principally associated with:
o: Stock-taking
The launch of the Doha Development Agenda
The formation of the G-33
The first adoption of the Singapore issues
x: MC7 in 2009 and MC8 in 2011, both held at Geneva, were primarily stock-taking conferences.
tq: Identify the common outcome of a paired conference entry.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MC9 — Bali — Trade Facilitation Agreement and interim Peace Clause on food stockholding
MC10 — Nairobi — Doha Development Agenda
MC11 — Buenos Aires — Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
MC12 — Geneva — Elimination of agricultural export subsidies
x: The Bali Ministerial Conference of 2013 produced the Bali Package, including the Trade Facilitation Agreement and an interim Peace Clause on food stockholding.
tq: Match the conference with its characteristic package while rejecting swapped outcomes.

s: The elimination of agricultural export subsidies was associated with the WTO Ministerial Conference held at:
o: Buenos Aires in 2017
Bali in 2013
Geneva in 2022
Nairobi in 2015
x: The Nairobi Ministerial Conference of 2015 adopted the outcome concerning elimination of agricultural export subsidies.
tq: Use the distinctive agricultural outcome to identify the correct conference.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the Eleventh WTO Ministerial Conference held at Buenos Aires in 2017?
o: It adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies and the COVID TRIPS waiver.
It extended the e-commerce moratorium to March 2026.
It produced no ministerial declaration and included a fisheries work programme.
It adopted a ministerial declaration and a permanent solution on public stockholding.
x: MC11 at Buenos Aires produced no ministerial declaration but included work on fisheries.
tq: Distinguish an absence of declaration from formal agreements at later conferences.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Twelfth WTO Ministerial Conference held at Geneva in June 2022:
1. The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted.
2. A COVID-related TRIPS waiver was adopted.
3. The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium was permanently abolished.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: MC12 adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies and a COVID-related TRIPS waiver. The e-commerce moratorium was extended, not permanently abolished, so statement 3 is false.
tq: Find the false later-development statement by separating extension from abolition.

s: At the Thirteenth WTO Ministerial Conference in Abu Dhabi in 2024, which of the following was the relevant outcome concerning the e-commerce moratorium and public stockholding?
o: The moratorium was extended to 31 March 2026, while no solution was reached on public stockholding.
The moratorium lapsed immediately and a permanent public-stockholding solution was adopted.
The moratorium was extended to 2030 and fisheries negotiations were concluded.
Both the moratorium and public-stockholding issue were permanently settled.
x: MC13 extended the e-commerce moratorium to 31 March 2026 but did not produce a solution on public stockholding.
tq: Compare two simultaneous outcomes instead of treating the conference as wholly successful or unsuccessful.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fourteenth WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde in March 2026:
1. It produced only a draft ‘Yaounde package’ and no ministerial declaration.
2. The e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026.
3. Sixty-six members signed a separate E-Commerce Agreement barring duties on digital trade.
4. A permanent solution on public stockholding was achieved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
x: MC14 produced no ministerial declaration, the e-commerce moratorium lapsed, and 66 members signed a separate agreement barring duties on digital trade. The permanent public-stockholding solution remained deadlocked, so statement 4 is false.
tq: Check each conference outcome separately and reject the over-claim of a settlement.

s: Which one of the following developments was associated with the WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde in 2026?
o: India blocked the addition of the Investment Facilitation for Development plurilateral agreement to Annex 4.
India proposed making the e-commerce moratorium permanent without opposition.
The Doha Development Agenda was launched.
The fisheries Phase 2 negotiations were concluded.
x: At MC14, India blocked addition of the IFD plurilateral agreement to Annex 4, although it had the backing of 129 of 166 members. Fisheries Phase 2 was deferred.
tq: Identify the relevant negotiating position while rejecting outcomes belonging to earlier conferences.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade is correct?
o: It was created by the Doha Ministerial Conference in 2001.
It ceased to have any relevance after the establishment of the WTO.
It was signed in 1947 and came into force in 1948 with 23 countries.
It was signed in 1948 and came into force in 1995 with 166 countries.
x: GATT was signed in 1947 and entered into force in 1948 with 23 countries. GATT continues as part of the WTO agreements even after 1995.
tq: Separate the founding history of GATT from the later establishment of WTO.

s: The Uruguay Round of multilateral trade negotiations is correctly described as the:
o: Sixth round, held from 1973 to 1979 with 23 contracting parties
Seventh round, held from 1980 to 1985 with 92 contracting parties
Eighth round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993 with 123 contracting parties
Ninth round, launched at Marrakesh in 1994 with 166 contracting parties
x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993, with 123 contracting parties.
tq: Verify round number, dates, venue and participation together.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the stated aims or areas of the Uruguay Round?
o: Opening of services trade
Reduction of farm subsidies
Coverage of investment and intellectual property rights
Establishment of a worldwide common currency
x: The Uruguay Round aimed to reduce farm subsidies, open services and cover investment and intellectual property rights. Establishment of a common currency was not its aim.
tq: Eliminate the unrelated policy objective from a list of negotiation aims.

s: The Dunkel Draft consisted principally of:
o: A schedule of tariff concessions adopted at Nairobi in 2015
Proposals by Arthur Dunkel for the Uruguay Round multilateral trade agreements
A declaration on fisheries subsidies adopted at Geneva in 2022
A treaty establishing the International Monetary Fund
x: The Dunkel Draft contained proposals made by Arthur Dunkel, the GATT Director-General and Chair of the Trade Negotiations Committee, for the Uruguay Round agreements.
tq: Link a named document with its author and negotiation context.

s: The Marrakesh Agreement of April 1994 resulted in which of the following?
o: Launch of the Doha Development Agenda in 2001
Creation of the WTO on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT system while retaining GATT as part of the WTO agreements
Creation of GATT in 1947 with 23 founding countries
Adoption of the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in 2022
x: The Marrakesh Agreement created the WTO, which began functioning on 1 January 1995. GATT continued as part of the WTO agreements rather than disappearing entirely.
tq: Distinguish institutional replacement from complete legal disappearance.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the World Trade Organization?
o: Headquarters — Geneva; Director-General — Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
Headquarters — New York; Director-General — Arthur Dunkel
Headquarters — Washington, D.C.; Director-General — Pascal Lamy
Headquarters — Paris; Director-General — Roberto Azevêdo
x: The WTO headquarters is in Geneva and its Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.
tq: Match the institution with its headquarters and current head without swapping officials.
sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

s: India’s status in relation to GATT and the WTO is correctly stated as follows:
o: India was a founding member of GATT but joined the WTO only after the Doha Round.
India was a founding member of GATT and became a founding member of the WTO.
India was not a member of GATT but became a founding member of the WTO.
India joined GATT after 1995 but was a founding member of the WTO.
x: India was a founding member of both GATT and the WTO.
tq: Test membership in both predecessor and successor institutions together.
sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

s: The WTO is commonly described as the third pillar of the world economy along with:
o: The IMF and the World Bank
The ADB and the OECD
UNESCO and UNCTAD
The ILO and WHO
x: The WTO is described as the third pillar of the world economy, alongside the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
tq: Recall the standard institutional trio.
sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

s: A country grants an advantage in customs treatment to one WTO trading partner. Under the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, it must generally:
o: Apply the advantage only to domestic producers
Extend the same advantage to other WTO trading partners
Extend the advantage only to countries with which it has a customs union
Withdraw the advantage from all trading partners
x: MFN requires non-discrimination among trading partners, so an advantage granted to one partner should generally be extended to other WTO trading partners, subject to permitted exceptions.
tq: Apply the non-discrimination principle to a trade-policy situation.
sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

s: Which situation best illustrates the national-treatment principle under WTO rules?
o: A country gives an export subsidy to domestic firms.
A country grants the same tariff concession to every foreign trading partner.
An imported product, after entering the domestic market, is treated like a similar domestic product for internal taxation and regulation.
A country imposes a quantitative restriction on all imports.
x: National treatment requires imported goods to be treated like domestic goods once they have entered the market, particularly in internal taxation and regulation. Equal treatment among foreign trading partners is the MFN principle.
tq: Separate national treatment from MFN by focusing on the point after importation.
sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

s: According to the WTO Global Trade Outlook of April 2025, India ranked what position in merchandise exports and had what share?
o: 10th position and 3.5 per cent
18th position and 1.8 per cent
15th position and 2.4 per cent
25th position and 1.0 per cent
x: India was ranked 18th in merchandise exports with a 1.8 per cent share according to the cited WTO Global Trade Outlook data.
tq: Match the rank and percentage as a single statistical pair.
sec: WTO basics - establishment, HQ, DG, India, MFN and national treatment  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to public stockholding for food security in the WTO, consider the following statements:
1. The Bali Ministerial Conference of 2013 provided interim protection under a Peace Clause.
2. The Peace Clause prevents legal challenges even when food-security procurement exceeds the limits prescribed under the Agreement on Agriculture.
3. India is seeking a permanent solution to the issue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: All three statements are correct. The Bali Peace Clause provides interim protection, while India seeks a permanent solution for its food-security procurement programmes.
tq: Combine three related features of a WTO arrangement and identify the option containing all correct statements.

s: Why does India's public stockholding issue under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture involve an outdated reference price?
o: Because the reference price is fixed by the World Bank every five years
Because MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is calculated using a historical reference price
Because the reference price excludes all procurement by government agencies
Because the reference price is based on the international price of food imports in 2013
x: India argues that MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is treated as an Amber Box subsidy using an outdated historical reference price.
tq: Test the precise technical detail behind a current policy controversy rather than its general description.

s: The negotiations on a permanent solution to the WTO public stockholding issue remained deadlocked at which Ministerial Conference?
o: MC11
MC10
MC13
MC14
x: The negotiations on a permanent solution to public stockholding remained deadlocked at the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference.
tq: Use the conference-number trap by distinguishing the latest ministerial meeting from earlier WTO conferences.

s: Which one of the following is NOT prohibited under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: Subsidies for fishing on unregulated high seas
Subsidies connected with inland fishing
Subsidies for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing
Subsidies for fishing in overfished stocks, unless rebuilding conditions apply
x: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. Aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.
tq: Find the excluded activity rather than selecting one of the prohibited forms of fishing support.

s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies applies primarily to which category of activity?
o: Only fishing undertaken within territorial waters
Only inland aquaculture operated by developing countries
Marine wild capture fishing and support provided at sea
All agricultural production connected with fisheries
x: The agreement covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. It does not generally cover aquaculture or inland fishing.
tq: Distinguish the positive scope of an agreement from nearby excluded sectors.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding special treatment under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies:
1. Developing countries and least-developed countries receive a two-year exemption in their exclusive economic zones.
2. The agreement provides for a Fish Fund to assist poorer members.
3. The exemption applies without any limitation to fishing on the high seas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The two-year exemption relates to fishing in the exclusive economic zones of developing countries and LDCs; it is not an unlimited high-seas exemption.
tq: Separate a limited territorial exemption from an incorrectly expanded high-seas exemption.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the recent status of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: It was adopted in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025.
It was adopted in 2025 and entered into force in September 2026.
It was adopted in 2013 and entered into force in 2016.
It was adopted in 2020 but has not yet entered into force.
x: The agreement was adopted at MC12 in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025.
tq: Check both the adoption year and the later entry-into-force date.

s: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is significant in WTO history because it is the first WTO agreement with which of the following objectives?
o: A military-security objective
A monetary-stability objective
A cultural-preservation objective
An environmental-sustainability objective
x: The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective.
tq: Identify the distinctive historical first associated with an agreement.

s: India became the 123rd WTO member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance for the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in:
o: June 2025
March 2026
September 2025
July 2026
x: India deposited its Instrument of Acceptance in July 2026, becoming the 123rd WTO member to do so.
tq: Combine a membership number with the exact month and year of a treaty action.

s: What was the immediate trade-related consequence of the lapse of the WTO e-commerce moratorium on 31 March 2026?
o: The moratorium was extended automatically for another decade.
All customs duties on physical goods were suspended.
The WTO prohibited digital imports by developing countries.
Developing countries lost tariff revenue on digital imports.
x: The lapse of the e-commerce moratorium exposed developing countries to the loss of tariff revenue on digital imports.
tq: Link the date of a policy change with its principal fiscal consequence.

s: The WTO e-commerce moratorium, which lapsed on 31 March 2026, had continued without such a lapse since:
x: The e-commerce moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998.
tq: Test the “first time since” date rather than the more prominent lapse date.

s: The principal reason for the paralysis of the WTO Appellate Body is that:
o: The WTO Agreement on Dispute Settlement Understanding has expired.
India has refused to nominate appellate judges.
The European Union has withdrawn from the WTO dispute settlement system.
The United States has blocked appointments to the Appellate Body.
x: The United States has blocked appointments, leaving the Appellate Body non-functional since December 2019.
tq: Use the “who exercises the blocking role?” approach in an institutional question.

s: The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since:
o: December 2019
December 2018
December 2020
December 2017
x: The Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019 because appointments have been blocked.
tq: Distinguish the precise start date of an institutional crisis from nearby years.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA)?
o: It is an EU-led stop-gap arrangement for appeals, and India has not joined it.
It is a compulsory arrangement to which all WTO members belong.
It is a fisheries agreement adopted by the WTO in 2022.
It is a permanent replacement for the WTO and is led by India.
x: The MPIA is an EU-led, 2020 stop-gap arrangement for appellate review during the Appellate Body crisis. India has not joined it.
tq: Discriminate between a temporary institutional arrangement and a permanent WTO body.

s: Which pair of WTO agreements is identified as the only two new agreements concluded in the last 30 years?
o: TRIPS and GATS
TFA and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
TRIMS and SPS
ITA and TBT
x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only two new WTO agreements concluded in the last 30 years.
tq: Start from the distinctive pair and eliminate agreements belonging to the original WTO package.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Agreement)
a. TRIPS
a. TRIMS
c. GATS
d. SPS/TBT
List-II (Subject)
i. Trade in services
ii. Minimum intellectual-property standards
iii. Investment measures affecting trade
iv. Food safety, plant and animal health, and technical standards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv
a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i
a–ii, b–i, c–iii, d–iv
a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii
x: TRIPS concerns minimum IPR standards, TRIMS concerns trade-related investment measures, GATS concerns services, and SPS/TBT concern health and technical standards.
tq: Start from the sure pair TRIPS–IPR and complete the agreement-subject mapping.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s: Which Indian law was enacted in 2005 to comply with the TRIPS requirement relating to product patents?
o: The Patents Act amendment of 2005
The Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999
The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001
x: India amended its Patents Act in 2005 to introduce product patents in accordance with TRIPS requirements.
tq: Match the legal enactment with the specific TRIPS-related compliance measure.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 — GI protection
2. PPV&FR Act, 2001 — plant varieties and farmers’ rights
3. Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 — food safety and standards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: All three pairs are correctly matched. These Indian enactments are associated with the relevant WTO-related compliance areas.
tq: Verify each law against its subject before selecting the all-correct combination.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s: India's compliance with TRIMS involved the:
o: Adoption of zero duty on all agricultural products
Introduction of compulsory export subsidies for all industries
Withdrawal from all investment-related commitments
Phase-out of local-content conditions affecting trade
x: TRIMS concerns investment measures affecting trade, and India's compliance involved phasing out local-content conditions.
tq: Distinguish a trade-related investment obligation from tariff and export-subsidy measures.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s: India's commitments under GATS are primarily associated with:
o: Zero duty on information-technology products
Liberalisation of trade in services
Regulation of illegal fishing subsidies
Protection of geographical indications only
x: GATS deals with trade in services, and India's compliance is reflected in its services-liberalisation commitments.
tq: Use the subject acronym to identify the corresponding area of WTO regulation.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is associated with India's compliance in the area covered by:
o: SPS/TBT
TRIMS alone
TRIPS alone
The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
x: SPS/TBT cover food safety, plant and animal health, and technical standards. India's Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is relevant to this area.
tq: Match an Indian statute with the WTO agreement category covering its subject.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) is correct?
o: It concerns services liberalisation, and India has not signed it.
It concerns geographical indications, and India joined the Lisbon Agreement.
It concerns zero duty on IT products, and India is a signatory.
It concerns public stockholding, and India ratified it in 2016.
x: The ITA concerns zero duty on IT products, and India is a signatory to it.
tq: Separate the ITA from the similarly abbreviated trade agreements and identify its subject and Indian position.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s: Which statement best describes India's position regarding the Lisbon Agreement on appellations?
o: India is a founding member but has suspended its membership.
India is a member and prefers it to TRIPS for GI protection.
India applies the Lisbon Agreement only to agricultural exports.
India is not a member and prefers TRIPS for GI protection.
x: India is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement on appellations and prefers to use TRIPS for geographical-indication protection.
tq: Discriminate between two international frameworks dealing with geographical indications.
sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

s: The Doha Round of WTO negotiations is also known as the:
o: Technology Round
Investment Round
Environment Round
Development Round
x: The Doha Round, launched in 2001, is known as the Development Round and covers agriculture, NAMA and services.
tq: Recall the distinctive informal title associated with a negotiating round.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the status and principal areas of the Doha Round?
o: It began in 1995 and was completed on agriculture alone.
It began in 2001, covers agriculture, NAMA and services, and remains unfinished.
It began in 2013 and covers only trade facilitation.
It began in 2022 and covers only fisheries subsidies.
x: The Doha Round began in 2001, is concerned with agriculture, non-agricultural market access and services, and remains unfinished.
tq: Check the year, scope and completion status together to reject partially correct alternatives.

s: The G-33 was formed in 2003 during the Doha process primarily to address:
o: Only information-technology tariffs
Fisheries subsidies in developed countries
Only intellectual-property protection
Food security, special safeguard mechanisms and special products
x: The G-33 is a group of more than 40 developing countries, including India, focusing on food security, the Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products.
tq: Identify the negotiating group's agenda rather than its membership alone.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Doha Round — Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies only
G-33 — African Group, ACP and LDCs
G-90 — Food security and special products only
NAMA-11 — Developing countries negotiating on non-agricultural market access
x: NAMA-11 is a group of developing countries, including India, concerned with non-agricultural market access. The G-90 consists of the African Group, ACP countries and LDCs.
tq: Use group-purpose matching and reject the swapped descriptions of G-33, G-90 and NAMA-11.

s: The G-90 comprises which of the following groups?
o: The African Group, ACP countries and least-developed countries
NAMA-11 members and fisheries-exporting countries
The European Union, Japan and the United States
India, China, Brazil and other emerging economies only
x: The G-90 consists of the African Group, African, Caribbean and Pacific countries, and least-developed countries.
tq: Test the composition of a country group using the membership trap.

s: In the WTO dispute concerning India's National Solar Mission, the subject of contention was India's:
o: Ban on imports of agricultural products
Fisheries subsidy exemption
Public stockholding programme
Domestic-content requirement for solar cells
x: The US challenged the domestic-content requirement under India's National Solar Mission in dispute DS456.
tq: Match the dispute name with the specific domestic policy measure challenged.

s: What was the outcome of the WTO dispute DS456 concerning India's National Solar Mission?
o: India won in 2016
The United States withdrew the complaint before a panel report
India lost in 2016
The dispute was settled through the MPIA
x: India lost the solar-cells dispute, DS456, in 2016.
tq: Distinguish the dispute number and subject from the outcome and settlement mechanism.

s: The WTO dispute DS541 involving India concerned which set of measures?
o: MEIS, SEZ and EOU schemes
The National Solar Mission alone
Steel safeguards imposed by the United Kingdom
The National Food Security Act and MSP procurement
x: DS541 concerned India's export subsidies under the Merchandise Exports from India Scheme, SEZ and EOU schemes.
tq: Use the dispute number to identify the cluster of domestic schemes involved.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the WTO proceedings concerning India's export subsidies under DS541?
o: The panel ruled for India in 2019 and the United States appealed to the MPIA.
The panel ruled against India in 2019, after which the matter was appealed into the void.
The dispute was decided in India's favour in 2023 by the Appellate Body.
The dispute concerned only India's fisheries subsidies and was withdrawn in 2021.
x: The panel ruled against India in 2019 in DS541, and the appeal went into the void because of the Appellate Body crisis.
tq: Combine the panel year, adverse finding and distinctive phrase describing an ineffective appeal.

s: The WTO dispute brought by Brazil, Australia and Guatemala against India related to:
o: Steel safeguards imposed by the United Kingdom
Domestic content in solar cells
Tariffs on ICT products under the ITA
Cane prices and export subsidies
x: The sugar dispute involved India's cane pricing and export subsidies. The panel ruled against India in 2021, after which the matter was appealed.
tq: Match the complainant countries with the commodity and policy issue in dispute.

s: Which countries were involved in the WTO dispute concerning India's duties on phones and other ICT goods in relation to the ITA?
o: The United States, Canada and Mexico
Brazil, Australia and Guatemala
The European Union, Japan and Taiwan
China, South Africa and Indonesia
x: The ICT-tariff dispute was brought by the European Union, Japan and Taiwan and concerned duties on phones and ICT goods vis-à-vis the ITA.
tq: Identify the complainants in a trade dispute from a group of plausible country combinations.

s: The WTO panel ruled against India in the dispute concerning ICT tariffs in:
x: The panel ruled against India in the ICT-tariff dispute in 2023.
tq: Separate the years of the solar, export-subsidy, sugar and ICT disputes.

s: In May 2026, India raised the United Kingdom's steel safeguard at the WTO body known as the:
o: Dispute Settlement Body only
Council for Trade in Goods
Committee on Trade and Environment
Trade Policy Review Body
x: India raised the UK's steel safeguard at the Council for Trade in Goods in May 2026.
tq: Apply the “which WTO body handles goods-trade measures?” approach.

s: India's steel exports to the United Kingdom in 2025–26 were valued at approximately:
o: $389.4 million
$593.4 million
$893.4 million
$1,893.4 million
x: India's steel exports to the United Kingdom were valued at $893.4 million in 2025–26.
tq: Use ascending numerical options and distinguish the reported trade value from nearby figures.

s: The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference held at Yaoundé in March 2026:
o: Adopted the Doha Development Round as completed
Issued a comprehensive declaration on all pending issues
Replaced the Appellate Body with the MPIA
Failed to issue a declaration
x: MC14, held at Yaoundé in March 2026, failed to issue a declaration.
tq: Test the outcome of the latest conference rather than its venue alone.

s: Which one of the following best describes India's concern regarding plurilateral initiatives such as the Investment Facilitation for Development and the E-Commerce Agreement?
o: They apply exclusively to agricultural subsidies and food security.
They may fragment the WTO system by moving away from consensus-based negotiations.
They would make the Appellate Body fully functional without appointments.
They would automatically abolish all WTO agreements.
x: India fears that plurilateral initiatives such as the IFD and E-Commerce Agreement may fragment the WTO by weakening the consensus-based multilateral approach.
tq: Apply the institutional principle of consensus to a contemporary negotiating debate.

s: Why are the WTO fisheries-subsidy rules of particular relevance to Andhra Pradesh?
o: They affect the interests of Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, who have sought a fisher-centric approach.
They prohibit all fishing activity along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
They concern only software exports from Visakhapatnam.
They directly regulate only inland irrigation projects in Andhra Pradesh.
x: The rules are relevant to Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, and Indian fisher bodies have sought a fisher-centric approach to their implementation.
tq: Connect an international policy issue with its concrete regional stakeholder impact.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is the first WTO agreement with an environmental objective.
2. The e-commerce moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998.
3. India joined the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: All three statements are correct. The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective, the moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998, and India joined the fisheries agreement in July 2026.
tq: Combine separate current-affairs facts and check whether the comprehensive option is supported by all three.
